explanation: The city was named after Constantine, but this building was Justinian's, raised in under six years. Its first dome partly collapsed after an earthquake in 558 and was rebuilt higher.

claims.text: The present Hagia Sophia was built under Emperor Justinian I and completed in 537.
Constantine the Great, Theodosius I and Charlemagne did not build the present Hagia Sophia.
Constantinople was named after Constantine the Great.
Construction of Justinian's Hagia Sophia took less than six years, from 532 to 537.
The first dome of Hagia Sophia partly collapsed in 558 after an earthquake and was rebuilt higher.

Hagia Sophia: Justinian Declared "I Have Surpassed Solomon" — Twenty Years Later the Dome Collapsed

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Sources date the collapse to May 7, 558, during a tremor that followed earlier quakes in 553 and 557. ... A Columbia note places the earthquake in December 557, with the collapse in 558. ... Justinian assigned the work to Isidore the Younger ... and raised the dome.

claimResults.note: Core of the claim confirmed: the first dome fell in 558 after earthquake damage and the replacement (finished 562) was higher. Sources differ on the quake year (557 or 558) and on partial versus complete collapse; see the note under issues.

issues.note: c5: sources agree the first dome fell in 558 and was rebuilt higher (completed 562), but they differ on the quake date (Columbia gives December 557; others a tremor on 7 May 558) and on whether the collapse was partial or complete. 'Partly' and 'an earthquake in 558' are safe only as hedges; 'fell in 558 after earthquake damage' is the form all sources share. Optional.
